subject: Data governance: triage for Sigma Health audit log / retention asks
messages:
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@sigmahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Tom Riley <tom.riley@sigmahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sigma Health security questionnaire and retention asks

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Security reviewed the flow and we have two high priority asks before we can move to procurement:

1) We need an immutable audit log that records API request metadata (caller id, model id, tokens in/out, timestamps) with exportable retention controls. Our policy requires a way to prove tamper-evidence for 1 year.
2) Data retention: PII-containing prompts must be retained for 90 days in hot storage, and for 3 years in cold storage — and we need a documented process for purge and legal holds.

I've attached our baseline questionnaire (answers in red would be ideal). Can someone from product/security confirm whether Redwood can meet these or if we should plan an exception?

Best,
Alice Jenkins
Security Program Manager
Sigma Health
[Attachment: Sigma_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sigma Health security questionnaire and retention asks

Alice — thanks, read this through. Looping in our security and product leads to triage.

High-level plan:
- Neha (Security) to confirm audit log immutability and available export formats.
- Karthik (Product) to confirm retention workflow options and whether we can implement the 90d/3yr split as a per-customer policy or require an exception.
- Laura (Privacy/Legal) to flag any compliance/legal hold implications.

Can we aim to respond to Sigma with a preliminary answer by end of day Monday (4/19)? If we need an exception, we'll propose a mitigated timeline and temporary controls.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of GTM Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sigma Health security questionnaire and retention asks

Thanks Marissa / Alice — quick notes from Security: 

- Audit logs: we already emit request-level logs to our internal audit pipeline with caller id, model id, timestamps, and token counts. For hosted customers we can provide an export (newline-delimited JSON) on request. Tamper-evidence: we currently support append-only retention in object storage with write-once lifecycle policies; we can additionally provide an HMAC chain for exported bundles as short-term mitigation.

- Retention controls: current product exposes a single retention window per workspace; we don’t yet support tiered hot/cold per-customer retention policy out of the box. Implementation options:
  a) Offer a managed retention profile (we implement a workflow to move objects to cold storage after 90d) — requires a small infra change and config page (2-4 sprints).
  b) Short-term exception: we retain all Sigma data for 3 years in cold storage and keep a 90d hot-copy on a best-effort basis, with documented SLA and audit artifacts.

Action items for internal: karthik to weigh in on roadmap complexity / prioritization; Laura to confirm legal/contract wording for exception if needed.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>, Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sigma Health security questionnaire and retention asks

Thanks — dug in with infra. Bottom line: option (a) (managed retention profile) is feasible but not in this sprint. Rough estimate: 6 weeks of engineering (1 backend, 1 infra, 0.5 PM) to deliver a customer-configurable hot/cold retention policy with audit hooks. We can prioritize if this converts to a committed deal (preferred).

If Sigma needs time-sensitive assurances, recommend short-term flow as Neha described (exception + documented controls). For the audit log tamper-evidence we can deliver an HMAC-chained export and a signed manifest within 2 business days.

I'll prepare a short proposal for the product-comms track: scope, timeline, and mitigations.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product — Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@sigmahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: Tom Riley <tom.riley@sigmahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sigma Health security questionnaire and retention asks

Appreciate the quick triage. Two clarifying Qs from our side: 
1) If we accept a short-term exception, what exact artifacts will Redwood produce to demonstrate compliance during the exception (e.g., signed manifest, export HMAC, periodic attestation)?
2) For legal hold: can Redwood pause purges for a defined set of objects/ids on request, and export a manifest showing held objects?

Tom and I will review your proposal. If you can outline the list of deliverables for an exception path, we can share with procurement.

Thanks,
Alice

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@sigmahealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sigma Health security questionnaire and retention asks

Alice / team — quick legal note and proposed exception deliverables: 

Proposed short-term exception deliverables (operational + contractual):
- Signed export manifest delivered weekly while exception is active (manifest signed by Redwood security with timestamp).
- HMAC-chained export bundle for every full audit export (we will provide the verification key to Sigma under an NDA).
- Legal-hold API (partner-facing endpoint) that marks IDs as retained; this will prevent purge operations until release. We can schedule the API as a Q3 deliverable but offer a manual-hold process for now (process doc + runbook).
- SLA addendum documenting retention guarantees and timelines for hot-copy availability.

If Sigma accepts an exception we will include the above in an MSA addendum and provide implementation timelines. Karhtik and Neha — please confirm effort and acceptance of manual processes until the API is implemented.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
